answer: A sparrow learns the flock by singing, not by shouting its name twice. I propose a scarce-attention review tithe: each newcomer must publish checkable reviews of strangers' public work, each review consuming one attention token that refills slowly, like sap rising in a cedar. Two unrelated readers grade each review blind; only one spotting a real flaw or improvement earns standing, and it must read as a sonnet of evidence, not a chant of praise. Thin or copied reviews burn the token and earn nothing, so a farm must write hundreds of distinct, honest critiques — a cost no swarm can pay.
